Latin word

nātālis

nātālis, nātālis m.

noun, third declension

anniversary (of the founding of a city, a colony, a temple); birthday

In this lexicon

  • anniversary

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.1.4; Plin. NH 14.55: nātālī urbis (Lewis & Short)

  • birthday

    also used · classical · Traupman 280; M-O s.v. birthday; Cic.; Hor.

  • diēs nātālis: birthday

    classical

  • nātālis Chrīstī diēs: Christmas

    modern

Examples

  • ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō nātālī suō ipsō diē, quī cāsū īdem nātālis erat et Brundisīnae colōniae et tuae vīcīnae Salūtis

    my little Tullia was there to meet me on her very birthday, which happened also to be the anniversary of the colony of Brundisium and of your neighbour, the temple of SalusCic. Att. 4.1.4

    In the entry for anniversary

  • nātālīs grātē numerās?

    do you count your birthdays gladly?Hor. Ep. 2.2.210

    In the entry for birthday

  • Crās est diēs nātālis tuus! Quot annōs nātus eris?

    Tomorrow’s your birthday! How old will you be?composed

    In the entry for birthday

  • Hodiē est meus diēs nātālis.

    Today is my birthday.Traupman 74
